title: The Yadavas of Devagiri
definition: A prominent medieval Indian dynasty (c. 850–1334 CE) that ruled the Deccan region, primarily modern-day Maharashtra, northern Karnataka, and parts of Madhya Pradesh, with their capital at Devagiri (Daulatabad).
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the political transition in the Deccan between the decline of the Chalukyas/Rashtrakutas and the advent of the Delhi Sultanate (Khaljis).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of The Yadavas.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
